name: Cycles in product
description: Consider a tree (that is, an undirected connected graph without loops) $$$T_1$$$ and a tree $$$T_2$$$. Let's define their cartesian product $$$T_1 \times T_2$$$ in a following way. Let $$$V$$$ be the set of vertices in $$$T_1$$$ and $$$U$$$ be the set of vertices in $$$T_2$$$. Then the set of vertices of graph $$$T_1 \times T_2$$$ is $$$V \times U$$$, that is, a set of ordered pairs of vertices, where the first vertex in pair is from $$$V$$$ and the second — from $$$U$$$. Let's draw the following edges: Between $$$(v, u_1)$$$ and $$$(v, u_2)$$$ there is an undirected edge, if $$$u_1$$$ and $$$u_2$$$ are adjacent in $$$U$$$. Similarly, between $$$(v_1, u)$$$ and $$$(v_2, u)$$$ there is an undirected edge, if $$$v_1$$$ and $$$v_2$$$ are adjacent in $$$V$$$. Please see the notes section for the pictures of products of trees in the sample tests. Let's examine the graph $$$T_1 \times T_2$$$. How much cycles (not necessarily simple) of length $$$k$$$ it contains? Since this number can be very large, print it modulo $$$998244353$$$. The sequence of vertices $$$w_1$$$, $$$w_2$$$, ..., $$$w_k$$$, where $$$w_i \in V \times U$$$ called cycle, if any neighboring vertices are adjacent and $$$w_1$$$ is adjacent to $$$w_k$$$. Cycles that differ only by the cyclic shift or direction of traversal are still considered different .
input_specification: First line of input contains three integers — $$$n_1$$$, $$$n_2$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le n_1, n_2 \le 4000$$$, $$$2 \le k \le 75$$$) — number of vertices in the first tree, number of vertices in the second tree and the cycle length respectively. Then follow $$$n_1 - 1$$$ lines describing the first tree. Each of this lines contains two integers — $$$v_i, u_i$$$ ($$$1 \le v_i, u_i \le n_1$$$), which define edges of the first tree. Then follow $$$n_2 - 1$$$ lines, which describe the second tree in the same format. It is guaranteed, that given graphs are trees.
output_specification: Print one integer — number of cycles modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 997D — Cycles in product [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
